steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Successful compositions show DEVELOPMENT, not just repetition — musical ideas are extended, varied, transformed and combined across sections. | Key Fact: Structural planning before composing: decide on form, key relationships, textural changes and dynamic shape — this prevents aimless meandering. | Key Fact: Contrasting sections create musical interest: vary texture (thick/thin), dynamics (loud/soft), harmony (tense/resolved), melody (legato/staccato). | Key Fact: Linking to Areas of Study strengthens your composition: use elements from your chosen AoS as inspiration for style, harmony and structure.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how composition techniques and development are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use composition techniques and development. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use composition techniques and development in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
